record.file_problem: none; full conference paper text supplied
record.tranche_reason: It measures training NLL and test error across image-model architectures, data sizes, and architecture variants to examine overfitting and generalization; these are conceptual tests of architecture and model-size conditions in the mapped claim.
record.gate_note: Reports results on natural image datasets, including training NLL/test error comparisons and loss-landscape measurements. The paper does not test random-label memorization, dropout, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, or magnitude-aware sharpness. Loss-landscape and feature-map measurements are included where they bear on a mapped version; figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures CNN–Transformer comparisons, attention locality, and loss geometry, rather than any specified claim version. V3 requires convolutional versus fully connected networks; Transformers and local-attention hybrids are different comparators. MLP-Mixer also has a structured patch/token architecture and is not the fully connected comparator specified by V3. Hessian eigenvalues and filter-normalized landscape visualizations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors interpret attention as spatial smoothing that complements convolutions, associate its benefits with flatter losses, and attribute poor small-data ViT performance to non-convex optimization rather than overfitting under strong augmentation. They report benefits from locality, multi-stage designs, and appropriately placed attention blocks. Their overfitting conclusion uses augmented-training NLL and clean-test error, rather than a directly measured training–test error gap.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AdamW, cosine scheduling, warmup, strong DeiT-style augmentation, stochastic depth, and 300-epoch image-classification training. Comparisons address architecture and loss geometry, not arbitrary-label memorization or controlled no-regularization training.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size and dataset (CIFAR versus ImageNet), MSA locality/kernel size, model family and stage structure, patch size, head count, training duration, classifier pooling, strong augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: CNNs outperform canonical ViTs on small CIFAR datasets; some local-attention Transformers outperform CNNs on ImageNet. ResNet-18 has 22.0% error versus 30.4% for ViT-S at broadly similar augmented-training NLL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative held-out performance of CNNs and vision Transformers depends on dataset scale and architecture under the tested training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Local attention improves ViT training NLL and test error relative to global attention; patch size and classifier pooling also affect performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention locality, patch size, and pooling influence ViT optimization and held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: ViT training NLL and test error both worsen as training data shrink and both improve with longer training under strong augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested augmented-training regime, poorer small-data ViT performance does not exhibit the authors' operational signature of overfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appropriately placed attention blocks improve ResNet accuracy and corruption robustness, while some placements reduce accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolution–attention hybrids can improve on CNN baselines, with benefits depending on attention placement.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian spectra and landscape visualizations vary with architecture, dataset size, head count, embedding dimension, model size, and training phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These design and training choices affect local loss curvature and visualized loss geometry; this does not establish magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps.

record.problems: No random-label experiment or direct measurement of train-test error gaps. Training NLL is measured on augmented training data, while test error is on clean test data. Many values are figure-only, with no uncertainty estimates stated. Models are trained with strong augmentation, stochastic depth, and AdamW, so findings do not isolate architecture alone.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for feature-map variance, Fourier-frequency analysis, corruption robustness, representation similarity, lesion-study accuracy changes, or detailed layer spectra: these are not the train/test generalization measures in V3 or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. Figure-only curvature findings are included where relevant to V3 but do not test V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, attribution to local connectivity in that comparison, learned sparse local connections, and convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD performance and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the large-batch penalty.
Controlled dropout effects, small-data failure, excessive-dropout underfitting, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with measured train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison against norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions because their measures or architecture comparisons do not identify those versions' effects. This does not dispute the reported findings. The record's V3 verdicts must be removed: it substitutes Transformers for fully connected networks and also assigns several verdict directions inconsistently with CNN superiority. Merely using AdamW, augmentation, or warmup does not test their corresponding claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Fully connected networks trained from scratch, sparse local connections, and convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance and tuning dependence.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with weight decay or data augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with the stated DeiT-style configuration; compared with ViT variants on test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Paper reports that stronger inductive bias lowers both test error and training NLL; precise ResNet-50 values are only plotted.
rows.check: ResNet versus Transformer comparisons do not establish the convolutional-versus-fully-connected effect in V3.

rows.subject: ViT-Ti
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with the stated DeiT-style configuration; compared with ResNet and other model families on test error and training NLL.
rows.note: The text says ViT does not overfit, and that stronger inductive bias lowers both test error and training NLL; on this small-data comparison ViT performance is inferior to CNNs.
rows.check: ViT is not a fully connected comparator. Its inferior performance against ResNet cannot be coded as a reversal of V3.

rows.subject: ViT-Ti
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated across subsampled CIFAR-100 training-set sizes; measured test error and training NLL.
rows.note: As dataset size decreases, both test error and training NLL increase; authors say the model does not overfit even at 2% dataset size.
rows.check: Subsampling ViT training data does not test any version; increased training NLL and test error do not measure V3.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ViT-S at similar training NLL on CIFAR-100.
rows.locator: Appendix C, Section “Rigorous discussion on the regularization of CNN’s inductive bias”
rows.note: The paper states that CNN inductive biases produce better test accuracy at similar training NLL.
rows.check: The reported 2.31 training NLL and 22.0% error are correct, but the comparator is ViT-S, not a fully connected network.

rows.subject: ViT-S
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ResNet-18 at similar training NLL on CIFAR-100.
rows.locator: Appendix C, Section “Rigorous discussion on the regularization of CNN’s inductive bias”
rows.note: ViT-S has lower training NLL but higher test error than ResNet-18.
rows.check: The reported 2.17 training NLL and 30.4% error are correct. ViT-S versus ResNet-18 does not test V3, and higher ViT error is not a reversal of CNN superiority.

rows.subject: PiT-Ti
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ResNet-50 on CIFAR-100 at reported training NLL and test error.
rows.locator: Appendix C, Section “Rigorous discussion on the regularization of CNN’s inductive bias”
rows.note: The paper says PiT accuracy is only 1.9 percentage point lower than ResNet; most CNN improvement is attributed to multi-stage architecture, not convolutional inductive bias.
rows.check: PiT is a multi-stage Transformer, not a fully connected network. The 1.9-point comparison is described against ResNet without an explicit model suffix in this passage; do not infer a uniquely specified baseline.

rows.subject: ViT with convolutional MSAs, kernel size 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Compared local convolutional-MSA kernel sizes on CIFAR-100 using test error and training NLL.
rows.note: The text says its training NLL is better than global MSA but worse than 5 × 5; test error is comparable to 5 × 5.
rows.check: Local attention kernel comparisons do not test convolutional versus fully connected networks. This overlaps R19, with a different baseline.

rows.subject: ViT with convolutional MSAs, kernel size 5 × 5
rows.operation_detail: Compared local convolutional-MSA kernel sizes on CIFAR-100 using test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Text states that 5 × 5 outperforms global MSA on training and test datasets.
rows.check: Local versus global attention does not test V3. Duplicate of R20.

rows.subject: ViT with convolutional MSAs, kernel size 8 × 8 (global MSA)
rows.operation_detail: Compared global MSA against local convolutional-MSA kernels on CIFAR-100.
rows.note: Global MSA has worse training NLL and test error than 5 × 5 kernel.
rows.check: Global versus local attention does not test V3. Duplicate of R21.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error and training NLL of ResNet and ViT families on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Text states both test error and training NLL of ViTs are inferior to CNNs on small-data CIFAR-10.
rows.check: CNN superiority over ViTs on CIFAR-10 concerns a different architecture comparison from V3.

rows.subject: ViT family models
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error and training NLL of ViT family models with CNNs on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Text states both test error and training NLL of ViTs are inferior to CNNs on small-data CIFAR-10.
rows.check: ViTs are not fully connected comparators; their inferior performance cannot establish a reversal of V3.

rows.subject: ViT with local MSAs
rows.operation_detail: Compared local-MSA ViTs and CNNs on ImageNet test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Text states both test error and training NLL of ViTs with local MSAs are superior to CNNs on large-data ImageNet.
rows.check: Local-attention Transformers outperforming CNNs does not test V3. Also, Appendix A.1 says ImageNet PiT and Swin use pretrained models, so the blanket trained-from-scratch condition is incorrect.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared with local-MSA ViTs on ImageNet test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Text states local-MSA ViTs have superior test error and training NLL to CNNs on ImageNet.
rows.check: CNN versus local-attention Transformer performance does not test V3; ImageNet PiT and Swin are pretrained according to Appendix A.1.

rows.subject: Alter-ResNet-50
rows.size_stated: ResNet-50 based; exact parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Replaced Conv blocks in ResNet-50 with local MSAs according to build-up rules; evaluated on CIFAR-100.
rows.note: Authors state Alter-ResNet outperforms CNNs even in small-data regimes; some third-stage MSA placements reduce accuracy while an MSA at the end of c2 improves it.
rows.check: AlterNet is a convolution–attention hybrid, not a fully connected comparator. This row also combines beneficial placements with detrimental third-stage placements.

rows.subject: Alter-ResNet-50
rows.size_stated: ResNet-50 based; exact parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared accuracy and corruption robustness with CNN and ViT baselines on ImageNet-1K.
rows.note: Authors state AlterNet's predictive performance is on par with Swin in accuracy; MSAs improve ResNet when build-up rules are applied.
rows.check: Hybrid architecture accuracy and corruption robustness do not test V3. Accuracy and corruption robustness should be separate measures.

rows.subject: ViT-Ti
rows.operation_detail: Training duration varied; measured training NLL and test error on CIFAR.
rows.note: Both training NLL and test error decrease as epochs increase; paper says ViT does not overfit even with many epochs.
rows.check: Training-duration effects do not test V3 or fixed-epoch batch-size effects in V5. Figure C.3 also includes ResNet, which outperforms ViT across the tested durations.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ViT-family models using Hessian eigenvalue spectra and loss-landscape visualizations.
rows.measure: loss curvature and Hessian eigenvalue magnitude
rows.value: smaller Hessian eigenvalue magnitudes for ViT; figure only
rows.note: This curvature measure is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7; the authors interpret it as flatter loss landscapes.
rows.check: Curvature does not measure V3 or V7. The row overlaps R22 and combines early-phase analysis with landscapes and spectra from several training phases.

rows.subject: ViT with GAP classifier
rows.operation_detail: Replaced CLS-token classifier with global average pooling; measured early Hessian spectrum and accuracy.
rows.measure: accuracy change and negative Hessian eigenvalues
rows.note: Authors state GAP suppresses negative Hessian max eigenvalues and improves accuracy by +2.7 percent point.
rows.check: The 2.7-percentage-point gain from GAP is reported correctly, but classifier pooling and Hessian changes do not test any version. Accuracy and curvature are separate measures.

rows.subject: Convolutional ViT, 3 × 3 kernel
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional-MSA kernel sizes; measured test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Text says 3 × 3 training NLL is better than global MSA but worse than 5 × 5; test error is comparable to 5 × 5.
rows.check: Local versus global attention does not test V3. Overlaps R7.

rows.subject: Convolutional ViT, 5 × 5 kernel
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional-MSA kernel sizes; measured test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Authors explicitly state 5 × 5 outperforms 8 × 8 global MSA on training and test datasets.
rows.check: Local versus global attention does not test V3. Duplicate of R8.

rows.subject: Convolutional ViT, 8 × 8 kernel (global MSA)
rows.operation_detail: Compared global convolutional MSA with local kernels; measured test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Global MSA is outperformed by 5 × 5 on training and test datasets.
rows.check: Global versus local attention does not test V3. Duplicate of R9.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Measured loss landscape curvature using top-5 Hessian eigenvalues on augmented training data with L2-regularized NLL.
rows.note: The paper reports ResNet has only a few negative eigenvalues while ViT has many, and smaller eigenvalue magnitudes for ViT; this is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: Hessian spectra do not measure V3 or magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance in V7. Overlaps R17; Figure 1 also covers later training phases.

rows.subject: ViT (dataset size 6%)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian eigenvalue spectrum with a reduced training dataset.
rows.measure: negative Hessian eigenvalues and positive-eigenvalue magnitude
rows.note: Figure and text say large datasets suppress negative eigenvalues; this is not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness.
rows.check: Dataset-size effects on Hessian spectra do not measure any version.

rows.subject: ViT with 2 × 2 patches
rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding patch size and measured CIFAR-100 test error and training NLL.
rows.note: Text says both very small and large patch sizes harm performance; 2 × 2 is the small-patch condition.
rows.check: Embedding patch-size comparisons within ViT do not test convolutional versus fully connected generalization.

rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding patch size and measured CIFAR-100 test error and training NLL.
rows.note: The figure compares patch sizes, but no exact 4 × 4 value is stated in text.
rows.check: Embedding patch-size comparisons within ViT do not test any version.

rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding patch size and measured CIFAR-100 test error and training NLL.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet local-MSA ViTs and AlterNet comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Local-MSA ViTs have better reported test error and training NLL than CNNs on ImageNet, and AlterNet improves ResNet; see R12, R15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100 architecture comparisons and local-MSA kernel sizes
reader_labels.reason: On small CIFAR data, standard ViTs underperform CNNs; local connectivity helps, while the advantage is conditional on kernel size and stage placement; see R2, R6–R9, R14, R19–R21.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 small-data model comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports CNNs outperform canonical ViTs on test error in small-data settings; see R2, R10, R11.
